categories.boundary_error: a word at a code-switch point (first word after a switch, or last before one) deleted or replaced
categories.deleted_speech: a run of deleted reference words (3 or more), speech that produced no output
categories.en_to_tl_substitution: an English reference word replaced by a Tagalog word or Tagalog spelling of it
categories.enclitic_particle: an enclitic or particle (po, naman, lang, na, pa, ...) deleted, inserted or replaced
categories.hallucination: a run of inserted words (3 or more), with no reference word behind it
categories.mixed_word_error: a Tagalog affix + English stem word (nag-meeting, i-share, naka-mute) deleted or mangled
categories.morphology_error: the right Tagalog root with the wrong or missing affix, reduplication or linker (-ng / -g)
categories.other_deletion: an isolated deleted word (fewer than 3 in a row) that no rule above explains
categories.other_insertion: an isolated inserted word (fewer than 3 in a row) that no rule above explains
categories.other_substitution: a substitution that no rule above explains
categories.proper_noun_error: a reference proper name deleted or replaced
categories.spelling_variant: the same word with another spelling or spacing; arguably not a recognition error
categories.tl_to_en_substitution: a Tagalog reference word replaced by an English word (by the output word's language, not the intent)

caveats: No reference token carries a word-level language tag, so every language label in this report is a heuristic guess from small hand-written word lists. Read the heuristic counts as indications, not as measurements of the speech.

The category counts depend on which of several equal-cost alignments is chosen. This report used the `default` tie-break (the one of eval/langscore.py, which the older tools use). The total never changes, but a category can move by tens of words under another tie-break (`--tie-break`; 67 words at most in the Liva check): do not read a difference of less than about 70 words in one category.
Hypothesis words are never tagged by a person, so tl_to_en / en_to_tl substitutions rest on a heuristic label for the hypothesis word even when the reference word is verified.

The word lists are small and were written by an AI model (Claude) without a native speaker's review: `unknown` is the largest honest answer for words they do not cover, and the ambiguous/unknown shares are reported rather than hidden.
Categories partition the word errors by a first-match rule list; a word that fits two rules is counted under the earlier one. Which rule fired is a design choice, not a linguistic finding.
When a reference interleaves speakers (overlapping speech) the words do not follow one time order, so some substitutions, deletions and insertions are ordering artefacts, not recognition errors.
